lesson_title: The Price Tag Behind the Price Tag: Scarcity and Opportunity Cost
hook_text: Every choice you make has a second, invisible price tag. Can you read it?
clip_script: Every choice carries two price tags. The first is printed and visible: three hundred rand for the boots. The second is invisible and heavier: what ELSE those three hundred rand would have become. Your genuine second choice was the gym month — so the TRUE cost of the boots is one month at the gym. Not three hundred rand. The money was leaving your pocket either way; the gym month is what you'll actually live without. Economics calls it opportunity cost, and once your eye learns to find it, it never stops. The Sunday car-wash shift banks one hundred and eighty rand — but in test season its hidden tag reads 'one afternoon of maths revision', and that tag can outweigh the cash. Even FREE things wear it: the free soccer clinic still costs the afternoon, and the afternoon had a next-best use of its own. That's the rule: the true price of anything is the next-best thing surrendered for it. Money reads the front of the tag. Your life is lived on the back of it.
visual_style: Slow-motion price tags flipping to reveal glowing hidden sides — a boot's tag flipping to show a gym card, a car-wash payslip flipping to show an open maths book, a 'FREE' sticker flipping to show a melting clock.
pacing: Steady flip-reveal rhythm, each flip landing a beat harder, closing cold on the front-and-back line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start reading both tags.
